name: Glibenclamide (Glyburide)
executiveSummary: Sulfonylurea (glyburide). Adult: start **2.5–5 mg PO/day** with breakfast; maintenance **2.5–15 mg/day** (usual max **15–20 mg**). High hypoglycemia risk — prefer alternatives in elderly/CKD. Not routine in pregnancy.
indications:
## Indications

- T2DM when diet/exercise/metformin are insufficient (less often first-line now).

## Precautions

- Prolonged hypoglycemia (long half-life) — risk in elderly, CKD, fasting, alcohol.
- Avoid if low CrCl; many guidelines discourage in >65–70 y.
- Interactions: ↑ effect with NSAIDs, sulfonamides, alcohol; ↓ with rifampin.

> Counsel on hypoglycemia symptoms; do not skip meals.

adulto.dose: Start **2.5–5 mg PO once daily** with breakfast. Titrate over days–weeks. Doses >10 mg: often split BID. Usual max **15 mg/day** (some labels **20 mg**).
adulto.administration: PO with food (first meal of the day).

neonatal.presentation: Not indicated (except monogenic neonatal diabetes — specialist).

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypoglycemia, weight gain, nausea, rash; rare: hematologic, photosensitivity.

bibliography.citation: ADA. Standards of Care — sulfonylurea hypoglycemia risk.
Beers Criteria / deprescribing in older adults.
